subject: Nebula Health — on‑prem/VPC readiness questions and checklist
messages:
From: Emma Wells <emma.wells@nebulahealth.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Jan 2028 15:24:00 -0800
Subject: Nebula Health - Private deployment kickoff / environment questionnaire

Hi Ben,

Thanks for taking this through. We're starting the procurement + technical intake for a private deployment of Redwood inside our datacenter (on‑prem) with a VPC‑like control plane. To get the SOW and timeline aligned, can you share the onboarding prerequisites and the specific environment validation steps Redwood needs from our infra team?

High level:
- Estimated nodes: 6 GPU hosts (NVIDIA H100 equivalent) in a single rack
- On‑prem network with dedicated interconnect to our colo provider
- Security: we need KMS integration (customer‑managed keys) and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM

Request:
1) A short checklist of account/procurement items and technical preflight items we should complete before the kick‑off call.
2) Any network diagrams or port/cidr requirements we should provide.
3) A sample runbook for the handoff and smoke validation you run during activation.

I've cc'd procurement (procurement@nebulahealth.com) who will need the contract summary and an expected timeline. Happy to get a 30–45m call on Monday if that helps.

Thanks,
Emma

Emma Wells
Head of Infrastructure, Nebula Health
emma.wells@nebulahealth.com
(415) 555‑0182

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Wells <emma.wells@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 06 Jan 2028 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nebula Health - Private deployment kickoff / environment questionnaire

Emma — thanks for the clear outline. We're excited to partner on this. Attached is a compact 'initial requirements' PDF that covers procurement artifacts we typically need and the technical preflight matrix. I'll summarize the immediate asks below and propose next steps.

Immediate checklist (short):
- Contract: signed SOW + ordering contact; populate procurement contact on the SOW
- Networking: primary CIDR for the private cluster; list of public egress IPs to allow; preferred BGP/route target if applicable
- Identity: service account owner, KMS ARN (or HSM details), and audit log forwarding endpoint
- Access: jump host IP(s) for our engineers during activation, and ticketing contact for SSH session scheduling

Technical preflight we need from Nebula infra team:
- Physical rack and switch details (bandwidth and MTU expectations)
- NTP servers, DNS resolvers, and any internal artifact repo endpoints required during bootstrap
- Expected peak and baseline token throughput estimates (so we can size concurrency/batching)

Attachments included: redwood-initial-reqs.pdf (compact procurement + preflight), and an editable port-matrix template. Karthik, Kim — copying you to validate the port list and any platform constraints.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick 30m tech sync Tuesday 10:00am PT — confirm?
2) Nebula sends network diagram + CIDR + KMS details before the call
3) We walk the runbook, then schedule a blocked 2‑hour activation window for smoke tests

Ben

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
(650) 555‑0124

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Emma Wells <emma.wells@nebulahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 07 Jan 2028 11:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nebula Health - Private deployment kickoff / environment questionnaire

Emma / Ben — quick technical proto‑check from the runtime/onboarding side. Below are the concrete items we need answered to avoid surprises during activation. I tried to keep it short and actionable.

Network & routing (must):
- Cluster CIDR and control plane CIDR (ex: 10.10.0.0/16 for compute, 10.11.0.0/24 for control)
- NAT/egress IP block(s) we can register for telemetry and license validation (we need stable egress IPs)
- Ports: 22 (SSH), 443 (TLS management), 2379 (etcd), 5000/6000 ranges for container runtime RPC — please fill the port-matrix template attached
- MTU: confirm whether jumbo frames are in use (we prefer 9000 for large transfers)

Security & keys:
- KMS/HSM: will Nebula provide an external KMS endpoint (TLS + client cert) or do we integrate with your in‑rack HSM? Provide sample key ARN or serial numbers.
- Audit logs: destination syslog/HTTPS endpoint + expected retention windows

Operational hooks:
- Jump host IPs for our ops sessions; we will not persist credentials and will rotate session keys after activation
- SNMP or telemetry pull endpoints for switch counters (optional but helpful for throughput tuning)

Sizing inputs we need ASAP:
- Concurrent sessions you expect (estimate: 10–50) and peak token rate per minute
- Expected model types (large decoder-only vs encoder‑decoder) — impacts memory/kv cache sizing

If you can drop answers into the port‑matrix and the attached short form, we can produce a lean activation plan. Happy to hop on the Tuesday slot Ben suggested.

— Karthik

Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
(415) 555‑0233

From: Emma Wells <emma.wells@nebulahealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nebulahealth.com, ravi.shah@nebulahealth.com
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 08:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Nebula Health - Private deployment kickoff / environment questionnaire

Thanks — attached is our network diagram and a completed port matrix (see attachments). Answers inline to Karthik's bullets:

- Cluster CIDR: 10.50.0.0/16 (compute), control plane: 10.51.0.0/24
- Egress IPs: 52.210.45.12 and 52.210.45.13 (we can reserve two for you)
- MTU: default 1500 on our colo; we cannot use jumbo frames at this time
- KMS: our key server is an on‑prem Thales HSM — attached is the connector spec and the HSM endpoint (will provide certs via secure upload)
- Audit logs: we will forward to splunk.nebula.internal:8088 with TLS and a shared ingestion token (procurement will provide the token via secure channel)
- Sizing: initial estimate 12 concurrent sessions, peak token rate ~30k tokens/min; planned models are mixture of LlamaX‑7B and some 13B variants

Procurement note (procurement@nebulahealth.com): we aim to finalize SOW by next Friday. Please share the SOW draft and any required redline windows.

Attaching: nebula-network-diagram.pdf and a completed port-matrix.csv. Will be on the call Tuesday with Ravi and our network engineer.

— Emma

Emma — this is great, thanks for the fast turnaround and the detailed artifacts. Quick summary and next actions so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of items received:
- Network diagram + filled port matrix (nebula-network-diagram.pdf, port-matrix.csv)
- KMS connector spec for Thales HSM (awaiting certs via secure upload)
- Egress IPs allocated: 52.210.45.12/13
- Sizing: 12 concurrent sessions; peak ~30k tokens/min; models: LlamaX‑7B / 13B variants

Planned next steps:
1) Tuesday 10:00am PT tech sync — confirm attendees (Ben, Karthik, Emma, Ravi, Nebula network engineer). We'll run the activation runbook and align the smoke tests.
2) Korn: we'll deliver a preflight checklist PDF (editable) post‑call with the exact timestamps for the activation window.
3) Procurement: Ben will send SOW draft to procurement@nebulahealth.com by EOD Friday; please confirm redline owners and any contract amendments required for HSM/KMS integration.

Preflight oral checklist highlights (what we will validate during smoke window):
- Control plane connectivity to HSM and successful key wrap/unwrap test
- KV cache priming with sample payloads and token echo checks
- Latency smoke: 95th percentile under target on small and medium prompts
- Audit log delivery to your Splunk intake with sample event and verified retention tag

Kimberly — can you coordinate the SOW dispatch and add a 2‑week redline turnaround on our template? Marissa — please prepare the preflight checklist and share the editable link.

Thanks everyone — appreciate the quick responses. Looking forward to the call.

Best,
Ben
